## Why This Is Asked
Tests precise bit-level reasoning across 128-bit boundaries without loops or conditionals. Evaluates clean use of bitwise operations across data word boundaries and edge-case handling.

## Key Concepts
- 128-bit composition as two 64-bit halves
- Bitwise AND for intersection detection
- Bitwise OR to combine half-results
- Zero-check inference for disjointness

```c
int isDisjoint128(uint64_t hi1, uint64_t lo1, uint64_t hi2, uint64_t lo2) {
  uint64_t m = (hi1 & hi2) | (lo1 & lo2);

}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests precise bit-mmask construction under edge-case shifts; no loops/branches is a common constraint in low-level systems.

## Key Concepts
- Bit masks and ranges
- Safe shifts with variable width (1..32)
- No branching; single expression mask composition

## Code Example
```javascript
uint32_t clearRange32(uint32_t x, unsigned a, unsigned b) {
  unsigned w = b - a + 1; // width of range
  uint32_t ones = (~0u) >> (32 - w); // w ones in LSBs
  uint32_t mask = ~(ones << a); // zeros in [a,b], ones elsewhere
  return x & mask;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to generalize to 64-bit with the same constraints?
- What if inputs are signed; does behavior change in C/C++?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of bitwise rotation, a common low-level primitive in systems and cryptography. 

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise rotation vs shift
- Normalizing k with k & 31
- Safe shifts using (32 - kk) & 31 to avoid 32-bit shifts

## Code Example

```c
uint32_t rotl32(uint32_t n, uint32_t k) {
  uint32_t kk = k & 31;
  return (n << kk) | (n >> ((32 - kk) & 31));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for 64-bit inputs?
- What are potential compiler/target differences in shifts?

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses pattern recognition and solid bit-twiddling under time pressure.

## Key Concepts
- Alternating bit patterns (0101..., 1010...)
- Using XOR with shifted version to collapse pattern
- Detecting all-ones masks with (x & (x+1)) == 0

## Code Example
```javascript
function hasAlternatingBits(n) {
  const x = (n ^ (n >>> 1)) >>> 0;
  return (x & (x + 1)) === 0;
}
```
